Inglewood, California
  February 4, 2020

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  February 4, 2020, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts/Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Wanda Brown  City Treasurer/Treasurer*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Franklin, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Dotson that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  January 31, 2020, in the amount of $4,047,536.85, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject the following claims filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) Bertha Del Carmen Aceves for alleged personal injury on June 1, 2019.
  2) Joannie Wilson for alleged personal injury on August 5, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Franklin, that
  the City Council does hereby reject the claims listed as A1-A2. The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  1
 February 4, 2020

 125  AMENDMENT ONE TO AGREEMENT NO. 19-302 APPROVED – MEYERS
  NAVE RIBACK SILVER & WILSON, PC; PAYMENT OF OUTSTANDING
  INVOICES FOR LEGAL SERVICES RENDERED AUTHORIZED. Staff report
  dated February 4, 2020, was presented recommending approval of Amendment One to
  Agreement No. 19-302 with Meyers Nave Riback Silver & Wilson, PC for expanded
  legal services and additional compensation.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment One to Agreement No. 19-
  302 in the amount of $500,000; and 2) Authorize payment of outstanding invoices for
  legal services rendered in an amount not to exceed $50,000. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 171  MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING AGREEMENT NO. 20-122 APPROVED
  – LOS ANGELES FOOD BANK. Staff report dated February 4, 2020, was presented
  recommending approval of a Memorandum of Understanding with the Los Angeles Food
  Bank, to support participation in the Older Adult Expansion Program.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby approve Memorandum of Understanding Agreement
  No. 20-122 with the Los Angeles Food Bank. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 183  APPROVAL OF USE OF THE AGREEMENT FORM CONSISTING OF 31
  PAGES WITHDRAWN; USE OF AGREEMENT FORM CONSISTING OF 3
  PAGES APPROVED - GRIFFITH COMPANY, INC. Staff report dated February 4,
  2020, was presented recommending two clarification actions be taken regarding the
  December 17, 2019 award of a Contract (Agreement No. 20-085) to Griffith Company,
  Inc. for the Transit Center Project for $5,480,500.00 (inclusive of the Contractor’s bid of
  $4,982,273.00 plus a 10% City controlled contingency of $498,227.00) per the terms,
  conditions and provisions of the Bid Documents for Bid No. CB-19-18.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Withdraw approval of the use of the Agreement
  Form which was before the City Council on December 17, 2019, as that Agreement Form,
  consisting of 31 pages (31 Page Agreement Form), was not part of the Bid Documents for
  Bid No. CB-19-18; and 2) Approve the use of the Agreement Form, consisting of 3 pages,
  which was a part of the Bid Documents for Bid No. CB-19-18 (3 Page Agreement Form).
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 301  PUBLIC HEARING SET – APPEAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION DENIAL OF
  SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-014 (SP-2019-014) TO ALLOW SALE OF BEER
  AND WINE FOR OFF-SITE CONSUMPTION FROM AN EXSISTING
  CONVENIENCE MARKET AT 400 WEST MANCHESTER BOULEVARD. Staff
  report dated February 4, 2020, was presented requesting that a public hearing be set to
  consider an appeal of Planning Commission Denial of Special Use Permit No. 2019-014
  (SP-2019-014) to allow the sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption from an
  existing convenience market at 400 West Manchester Boulevard.

  Mayor Butts set the public hearing for February 25, 2020, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  2
 February 4, 2020

  219  REPORTS – CITY TREASURER. City Treasurer, Dr. Wanda Brown, thanked
  Council Member Dotson, and Council Member Franklin for meeting with her to discuss
  the finances of the City. She spoke with Congresswoman Maxine Waters who stated that
  the numbers from the net assets/unrestricted fund balance were obscene and very serious.
  Dr. Brown stated that she agrees with the article written by John Marlick. Dr. Brown
  also commented that she feels it will be unlikely that the City will be able to overcome
  $450 million dollars unrestricted net balance. She explained that the $450 million dollars
  represent regular fund dollars that are unencumbered or no claims to, after all bills are
  paid.

  Dr. Brown also clarified that had she known a City employee would have been the first
  person drawn to qualify for the 1st Time Home Buyer’s Lottery, she would not have
  participated. She stated that since the last City Council meeting (January 28, 2020), she
  has received over 36 telephone calls regarding the Home Buyers Lottery, and one in
  particular from former Los Angeles Police Chief, and Council Member Bernard Parks
  who was concerned with the City of Inglewood First-time Housing Program. Lastly she
  stated that she will be offering free income tax services to retired senior citizens ages 55
  years and older that live in the City of Inglewood starting February 10, 2020 until March
  31, 2020.

  127  MAYOR BUTTS REMARKS. Mayor Butts asked Sharon Koike, Assistant Finance
  Director, about information regarding the CAFR, and how net asset/net liabilities are
  calculated. She stated that $266 million dollars is in the PERS unfunded liability. Mayor
  Butts stated that the $266 million dollars is an estimate that PERS make every 2 years. It
  is based on what it would take to fund the retirements for every one that is retired right
  now, and until they die, and everyone that is working that would retire assuming they
  would retire, until they die. Mrs. Koike confirmed that if everyone working for the City
  of Inglewood retired today, along with those that are already retired, $266 million dollars
  would be what the City would pay for their retirement and perpetuity. However, everyone
  that is employed with the City of Inglewood today, isn’t retiring tomorrow. She also
  confirmed that the $266 million dollars is only a projected estimate given if the stock
  market changed and PERS receives over and above the 7% that they projected.
  Additionally, Mayor Butts inquired if the Bond rating agencies base their credit
  worthiness on projection or the City’s ability to fund the retirement system. Mrs. Koike
  confirmed that credit worthiness is based on the ability to fund the retirement system.
  Mayor Butts asked if the City has missed any retirement payments. Mrs. Koike stated no
  the City has not. Mayor Butts furthered inquired how many bond ratings has the City of
  Inglewood had? Mrs. Koike stated the City of Inglewood has had four.

  Mayor Butts stated that the Bond Agencies are the true barometer of credit worthiness for
  the City. He also stated that the Bond Agencies decide at what level a City is able to
  borrow money. Mayor Butts inquired if the City of Inglewood is in danger of being
  insolvent. She commented no. Mayor Butts asked if Moody’s has rated the City of
  Inglewood from time to time as the most liquid city in the country. She confirmed this
  was correct. Mayor Butts inquired if any of the rating agencies have expressed concerns
  about the City’s solvency and credit worthiness. Mrs. Koike answered “No, they have
  done the opposite”. Mayor Butts stated when he took office, the city’s rating was a
  –BBB, he then asked Mrs. Koike what is the City of Inglewood’s credit rating today, and
  she stated –AA.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Stuart Bailey thanked the City Council Members for holding their holiday toy drives for
  the residents of Inglewood residents.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in memory of Kobe Bryant, Gianna Bryant, and the other persons aboard who
  lost their lives in the tragedy at the hour of 2:31 p.m.

  3
 February 4, 2020

  Approved this 25th day of February, 2020
